name: Building Tools
comment: Where Building Tools finds game code by its bytes, wherever Kiln has a symbol on those bytes (and two more: MissingCall, ScreenDispatch). It loads as a dinput8.dll proxy, a Kiln Library native mod or mods/building-tools/BuildingTools.dll (ShroudForge, XHL-Core), starts a thread from its DllMain, waits 4 s and scans the live code once (exact signatures; jump-tolerant ones accept another mod's jump in their first `head` bytes and chain to it), then redirects the game's calls to what it found. Kiln code on an exact signature's bytes when it scans turns that feature of Building Tools off. Every Kiln symbol on a scan's bytes is listed under `kiln` with what Kiln does there; OPEN marks a known conflict. tools/sigport/tests/test_foreign_scans.py checks this on the pinned executables (docs/kiln/engines/README.md, 'Mods that find game code by its bytes').

kiln.ui/ChestFooter: OPEN (rare, not moved in 0.2.0-dev.31.13): kiln-core's native chest entries hook this entry when a mod first adds a chest button (Ui native chest entries). Only a hook that goes in before Building Tools' scan (a mod adding a chest button within Building Tools' first 4 s) turns its menu, wheel and exact window off; after the scan both work. Not moved because the hook counts the footer's nesting around the whole call (it needs the function's end as well as its start) and the function is split into several code chunks, so a pair of mid hooks inside it is not a small change

kiln.build/BlueprintApplyRet: not hooked: the return address kiln-items compares ApplyMaterials' caller with. Building Tools redirects this call and the other building programs' calls of ApplyMaterials (PayCost) to its own code, which then calls ApplyMaterials, so Kiln's hook there sees its DLL as the caller. Since 0.2.0-dev.31.13 kiln-rules (BuildCost, BuildRefund) and kiln-items (building-link payments) find the game's call behind it on the stack (native/core/abi/kiln_call_site.hpp) and decide by that call; a payment they cannot trace stays the game's, logged once per module. Until then those rules did not apply while Building Tools ran (from its code, not seen in a game)

kiln.build/StockCount: not hooked: the call target kiln-items checks next to build/CursorStockRet (its mid hook is in the material check, not here)

kiln.stations/BaseStockForPlayer: not hooked: kiln-items calls it and checks its code before the crafting preview

kiln.rules/ApplyMaterials: hooked at its entry (kiln-rules' building costs, kiln-items' building links); Building Tools accepts a jump there (find_hookable, 7 bytes) and chains to it. Its redirected calls of it reach Kiln's hook from its DLL; see PAY_PLACE for how Kiln finds the game's call behind them
